<meta>This page continues a linguistic and philosophical analysis of Hebrew grammar, specifically focusing on the concepts of "deficiency" and "excess" in speech and action.</meta>

The explanation of those instances where "He is gracious" <note>Hebrew: *ki yachon*</note> appears nine times, and those which occur for its sake; and their **grammar** <term>dikduk: the systematic study of the rules of the Hebrew language</term> still stands within them without **addition** or **deficiency**. And this is because actions in the Hebrew language are performed in two ways: one of them is the action of utilizing weariness <note>possibly referring to physical labor or effort</note>, and the other is the making and the speaking of a name regarding the doer. 

And behold, in that which is in speech and from speech, there were a minority of the creative works <term>melachot: purposeful activities or crafts</term> that emerge from the verse. And so it is with a name and a word: three hundred and thirty expressions of speech between the heart and the ear. And these are but words, except that their improvement and their meaning shall be given. For its explanation is that the matter is undoubtedly an obligation; and their opposites are **iniquity**, **injustice**, and the separation of meaning. 

And this is the matter of a verb that is not obligatory, found in crafts that are deficient but correct—that is, "deficient" <note>Hebrew: *chaser*</note> and "deficient speech." All of these exist in the partition between the soul, the ear, and speech. And these are the secrets of this **deficiency** and **excess** from our inner depths. For "making" was separated in them by these words: **sin** and **injustice**. 

And the nicknamed words are the "correction," for their matter is a deficiency of meaning, yet the error is not in its intention—that is, "deficient" and "injustice." And the attributes of deficiency and improvement are literally according to its "mouth" <note>idiomatic for "expression"</note>, and there is no other interpretation for it; on the contrary, these are the goodness of the Scripture for the rebuke of the deficient. And in those things done with a minority of action—for the individual is "deficient-full"—these are thus, even in a metaphorical way through which they return to him. And between these, speech and literature are a matter for him regarding the root of speech.

<summary>This page provides a grammatical and philosophical treatise on the nature of Hebrew words, distinguishing between actions of labor and actions of speech while exploring the moral and linguistic implications of "deficiency" and "excess." It categorizes terms like sin and injustice as linguistic deviations that reflect deeper spiritual or intentional states.</summary>

<keywords>grammar, deficiency and excess, speech vs action, iniquity, injustice, Hebrew roots, linguistics, philosophy of language</keywords>

# The Secret of Formative Man

And when it ascends from the aspect of the mystery of *Malchut* <note>The lowest Sefirah, "Kingship," representing the manifest world</note> and within it there are two, etc., there is the name of *Malchut*. And as I have written in my knowledge regarding the matter of these angels in the aspect of *Binah* <note>Understanding</note>, except that it is a mystery. And here, the *Yesod* <note>The Sefirah of "Foundation," associated with procreation and connection</note> are natural, etc., and the change of the unification, etc., sometimes with the well-known partner <note>The feminine aspect of the Divine</note>, or sometimes natural in the mystery. And this is the Name of Four Letters <note>The Tetragrammaton: Y-H-W-H</note> which is sufficient, and they are the Four Faces: the face of a Man, the face of a Lion, and the power shall be through the tenth, twice. And they are the supreme couple called **Adam** <note>Man</note>. Also, **Adam** has four levels of glory which are twenty-eight <note>The numerical value (Gematria) of the Hebrew word for "Power" (Koach) is 28</note>. And all around these are the Face of Man, which is *Malchut*, and they are the Four Living Creatures <note>The *Chayot* from Ezekiel's vision</note> in the stone <note>original: "eben"</note> S-T-K-A <note>Likely a cipher or acronym for divine names</note> Y-H-W-H, etc. That is to say, the angel Uriel and Michael, which are the Right and North faces and the interior, etc. His intention is in the name *Adonai* <note>Lord</note> and in the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note> and in the name *Yahweh* in unifications, and may our prayer be upon it. The holy Ox, which is the mystery of Joseph and David who complete the union. And so the ancient sages said: for the flesh of Potiphar's building was complete, lacking only this, but "The Lord was with Joseph" and the Judges of Israel. And this is the Land of Righteousness, a name sufficient for a complete intention in *Yesod*. And this is the mystery of "My Pious One," righteousness and charity in *Yesod*, and this is the sign of *Yesod*, and regarding it he says: "The Lord God of Hosts." And the intention is through the unification and the flow of Leah through *Yesod*, and with Leah to "The Lord of Hosts" explicitly. And after the prayer on the seventh day in weeping, which is with her in *Yesod* in the mystery of the Holy Lord.

# The Secret of Formative Man

And behold, the perfection of the ten words of the staff, and they are the mystery of the Four Holy Living Creatures. And within them is the mystery of *Binah* which is "Man," where Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge <note>The triad of Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at</note> are concerned. And it is known that the daughter of *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> and *Malchut* make four Living Creatures. And behold, in this is included fourteen signs and accompaniments which are *Netzach, Hod, Yesod* <note>The lower triad of Sefirot</note> and the Sapphire Splendor, which are in the supreme place by the decree of the unification of the other companions who join and connect, who perform and lead the lower realms now in expression. And my intention here is not the angel of mercy as before, but rather there is:
-> Behold, in the words of the Pious ones (peace be upon them) regarding the Blessed God who is between them. <-

**However**, the crown of the day is intended only for the waters from the second standing in the soul of the fringed garment <note>The Tallit</note> that attains atonement. And it has already been rectified; if so, they were "slain" according to the number of this recognized combined total. Behold, the atonement is the high service through which one is atoned. And so there shall be a cleansing on the right in every intention, and that is toward the Four Living Creatures of His face: the three creatures of the Lion, the Right, and the Scorpion <note>Often substituted for the Eagle in certain astrological/kabbalistic contexts</note>. For he is the form in the place of all holiness. And the nourishment is the Wisdom and the life-force of the "Royal Father" <note>Abba</note> with Y-H-W-H. And now we shall come, as it were, according to the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note>, to the mystery of the Chariot <note>Merkavah</note> from the complete Y-H-W-H, etc. For from this combination of the names of the Living Creatures and between the body of the Living Creatures who are mounted in the simple mystery, etc.

# Gate of Life

It is further stated in the gloss: behold, regarding that additional letter *Heh* <note>The letter Heh (ה) often symbolizes the feminine presence or the Shekhinah in Kabbalah</note>, this *Heh* is the "heel" <note>original: *akevah* (עקבה), referring to the lowest point or the end of a structure</note>, and they are within the secret of the **Right** and the **Left**. In this, the letters *Yod-Heh* are on the Right and the *Heh* is on the Left. This follows the secret of *Yod-Heh* as mentioned regarding the back of the illustration:

-> **YHVH** over **ADNY** <-
-> and likewise **YHVH** of **AHYH** <-

And for this reason it is said, *He has made a memorial for His wonders* <note>Psalm 111:4</note>, and the addition of the *Heh* is "He has made" <note>The Hebrew word 'Asah' (made) ends with Heh</note>. This refers to the **Masculine** over the **Feminine** in two aspects. In the final Feminine aspect, *Yod-Heh*—which is to say *AHYH*—is over *ADNY YHVH*, and *ADNY* is over *YHVH*. Thus, "upon her" in the verse of the visions <note>referring to Ezekiel's vision</note> means the "heel" is over the Masculine.

How shall it be on the Right? The numerical value <term>Gematria: a system where Hebrew letters have numerical values</term> of **Kindness** <note>Chesed = 72</note> is over the diagonal *Heh*. Then "He made"—which is the aspect of Lordship (*Adnut*)—comes first, meaning the Pure one turns toward the Left of the Right. Afterward, on the Right, he turns toward his servant and passes him over her, and it becomes **Masculine**. On the Left, *ADNY* is first, which is in the second position from the Right to the Left, the Godly, and she passes him over, and it is "upon him," becoming the "heel."

Therefore, *the nations shall be glad and sing for joy* <note>Psalm 67:5</note>, for the union is in the Right and the Left, through **Direct Light** and **Returning Light**. The offspring are **Male** and **Female**, and it is impossible with fewer than three. For this reason, it is impossible to unify, elevate, and draw down the blessings unless the union is complete—**Male** and **Female**—who are the "branches" through which the individual details are acted upon, as explained in the book *Plantings of Pleasantness* <note>Netai Na'amanah</note> and in the *Book of Intention* <note>Sefer HaKavanah</note>. This shall be according to the secret of the "Table" mentioned previously, for the preparation is in the book *Netai*, and in another matter regarding the secret of "He shall be" (*Yihyeh*), where the letter *Aleph* is missing, and "Holy shall be..."

---

...the extra [letter] in the **Crown** (*Keter*), for you shall say the secret of *Yod-Heh-Heh-Vav-Heh*, which is entirely *Yod-Heh* as we have explained. These are established for all days, and the addition—how good and how pleasant is the duty of the day, as

-> we shall explain with the help of God: <-

The two external forces, "Mighty" and "Valiant," are her nature. To Him, in faithfulness, she woke me, and it was as the scripture said: *And he shall make atonement for himself and for his house* <note>Leviticus 16:6</note>. "In this" refers to his wife. It is known that the Zealous God <note>El Kanna</note> regarding forbidden relations hides His face, but with favor or His love, He is a "Fortress," as explained in the section "He shall be taken."

The reason for this is that "In this" rises [in value] to "Fruit" <note>Both 'Be-Zot' and 'Pirecha' equal 410</note> toward the Man. Since the two "Amens" came and they sinned, the Prince of this wrapping [seeks] to hide the deficiency. For "The House" is the "Back," because the souls of Israel are emanated from the **Divine Presence** (*Shekhinah*). Thus they are joined together in the secret of **Unification** with **YHVH**. He completed them and acquired her surroundings. The secret is:

**Masculine** toward the **Nothingness** (*Ayin*).
In the **Feminine** toward the **Left**.

Between the Right, he unified over the Left. In the Feminine, the Left passed over the Right. Therefore, the "Evening" of the Feminine has the numerical value of "Light" <note>Erev = 272; Or = 207; the text suggests a mystical equivalence</note> which ascends to her soul, and it becomes Female. Afterward, the pillar of the Masculine light goes forth and she gives birth to males. Their secret is *Netzach* and *Hod* <note>The emanations of Victory and Splendor</note>. Gentleness comes first, then a male child is born—a gathering of the strength of **Mercy** over **Judgment**. Through Him, the pious ones loved my will. In the end, it goes straight, for the Male prevailed over the Female. But when it is [reversed], it is Kindness—the strengthening of Judgment over Mercy.

# Section 2

For the power of Unification <note>Hebrew: *Yichud*, the mystical process of declaring and revealing God's oneness</note>, excellence, and strength are the blessings included within the All. Regarding these matters, there are hidden paths and other places where things require settlement and explanation. This matter is intertwined in the book with the "Letters of Governance" <note>referring to the mystical belief that the Hebrew letters govern the forces of creation</note>, and we shall write further concerning its strength in the secret:

Regarding the supervision of the seven days: before the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>, they would separate him <note>the High Priest</note> from his home. His preparation was pure for him, he was sanctified, and they would separate him from his wife for seven days. This was not merely due to the sin of ritual impurity <note>Niddah</note>, God forbid, for such has no dominion or confusion over him, unless he sinned through a peace offering or was negligent in the service of the days. During these seven days, they would sprinkle [purification water] upon him and give him tasks so that he would be accustomed, expert, and alert. This was done so that the service of that day <note>the Yom Kippur liturgy</note> would be weighty and precious to him, and behold, he is prepared and refined so that he may be capable. 

Likewise, on the eve of the Day of Atonement in the morning, they would pass before him bulls, rams, and lambs, so that he would be familiar and accustomed to the service until the matter of his separation was finalized. However, you should know that this obligation stands for the "peace offerings of flesh" <note>physical sacrifices</note> which belonged to that generation. But if one comes to the place of service where they are raised and made similar, and their actions every day required the exertion of the Name (may He be blessed), why? Because His will is that there be settled mind and the holiness of the Book.

<column-break/>

From it, and through many steps, until things are forbidden; and from it, in this structure, the one who serves Him. It is established in the "Holy Version" in our generation that we do not pass [animals] according to requests, nor do we engage in [physical] governance, perhaps until the Ancient of Days <note>A Divine title from the Book of Daniel</note> shall appear and be seen by the Lord.

However, regarding the reason for the Passover <note>likely a scribal error or specific mystical comparison to the transition of time</note>, these seven days are mentioned as seven watches until nine; for the purity from forbidden unions on the Day of Atonement is eight, which is restful for him. Know that a Great Man <note>Adam Rav</note> who is "One" in the chambers of the city is "Eighteen," which is "Ten," for they are called the Ten Days of Repentance <note>Teshuva</note>. Repentance is the sphere of Understanding <term>Binah: the third of the ten Sefirot, associated with the "Divine Mother" and the source of repentance</term>, and these ten days are the ten days in which the ten Emanations <term>Sefirot: the ten attributes or channels through which the Divine interacts with the universe</term> etc. 

However, the cause of Repentance—its explanation is known: the return of things to their Root <note>Shorasham</note> in the secret of the Jubilee <note>The 50th year in the Torah when slaves are freed and land returns to its original owner; mystically associated with the return of the soul to its source</term>. The matter is that the inclination turns toward Understanding without doubt, and the fleeting lives in every inclination are its existence and its very essence. However, some of them are in the secret of the letter *Yod* <note>the numerical value 10</note>, the Supernal Days. According to a man's action in those lives, so are their days within their days. Life is counted among the good things in the dwelling of our soul; in our sitting, we served Him. For behold, the praise today is that we are before the fulfillment of His service, His return, and His faith in Him. This is the secret of the Eight, corresponding to every day. This is the secret of "And the Children of Israel called to the day and it drew near" etc. David said: according to how he conducted himself in the Splendor <note>Hod</note> of faith, He drew near to him; and the Tenth is known as the Pious One.

# 12
<margin>7</margin>

To conduct an inquiry into the movement of the days and what they obligate a person toward themselves, so that every person may examine their own mind regarding life. However, regarding these matters, a sage who was held in high esteem by them said—and the words of Rabbi Jonah the Pious <note>Rabbi Jonah Gerondi (c. 1200–1263), a Spanish rabbi and moralist</note> in the book ***The Gates of Repentance*** are precious in this regard—that this [spiritual work] is equal in value to all of one's other affairs. And he said these things against the pious man and the one who busies himself with contempt for some of the sins of other days, while I feared for the rest of the days as well. This is the "ring of days" which I have separated in order to reveal today, out of seven days, that in the root of this day, one should understand his own mind and intellect, etc.

Thirdly: All the deeds of the days are those from which an obligation arises for man. And now, mix the Name of God <note>original: "Y-H"</note> with repentance, and you shall not be able to sin. It is a great kindness that God created the heavens and the earth and gave them the power to exist; and if they [the days/elements] were to consume them, and we were to become the holder of flames, He would know them all... <note>The text here uses cryptic abbreviations: KGM, AB, ChM</note>. There is no doubt that those who act according to their law in these matters, being in a state of chance <note>term: "Keri" (accidental/impurity)</note> and so forth, [should place] their wonder in a high place. And as you have seen much, the truth of the Sages will appear to him in this place—a grain of the awesome intellect, and also the full likeness of Man. And man shall truly see, as he is raised to the level of He who made these, how much pleasure there is in the deed and the obligation. And you already know that Man, etc.

# 13

The days and the inquiry: The Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to Israel the Ten Days of Repentance—days of return—so that first the inquiry, which depends on the days (which are the Ten, and the future), might take place. And they [the days] are his "taste" <note>or "reasoning"</note>. And the [letters] *Bet* and *Chet* of Repentance <note>original: "Teshuvah"</note> and Passover, which are in the life of the World to Come, and in the remainder they clung... Abraham... even though his repentance was as it should be. And here too, regarding the reason for atonement and the purity of the days through the [letter] *Bet*, which is so: the Ten Days of Repentance. And on the day of the heart, and goodness, and the qualities... in the secular book <note>or "the book of Chullin"</note>... Sotah... in the scripture, it is the secret of **The Great Sabbath** <note>The Sabbath immediately preceding Passover</note>.
<margin>Missing</margin>
And there is no "secular" in it at all. And likewise, the physical manifestation of the good, the purity, and the faith... to him all the days which passed in the desires of the time. It is proper for him to [distinguish] between his repentance and their purity, and to be unique in Sabbath and atonement and the nullification of the secular. However, the three days of Rosh Hashanah <note>The Jewish New Year</note> are "Good Days" <note>term: "Yom Tov" (Festival days)</note> as is known. And so, after it is done, and we occupy ourselves after the Festivals, they were the "found" days, and outside of them. And there is no doubt they are meritorious, for the ten days of Sukkot <note>The Feast of Tabernacles</note> and the liturgical poetry in this place indicate the holiness of the seventh... they guarded, and they shall say there is a "before" which indicates their holiness. And from them, in the version of "on such and such a day," etc. And also that which we were enticed by—that truth we have cast away; and through our iniquity and our sins, so that he may be blessed in those lives which he sustained for the sake of blood, etc. And the teaching of what he sustained, for that which he sustained in the days of Repentance... and if it were... they are the days of their trembling, the [Day of] Atonements.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exposition of the Sefirot, specifically discussing the relationship between Yesod (Foundation) and Chesed (Kindness). It builds on the previous page's themes of repentance and spiritual purity by explaining how these divine attributes facilitate the sacred union of the divine realms.</meta>

He is called the **Best Man of the Queen** <note>original: "Shoshbin de-Matronita," an Aramaic term for the Sefirah of Yesod acting as an intermediary for the Shekhinah</note>. Through him, it is known that <term>Yesod|Foundation; the ninth Sefirah and the channel of divine procreation</term> is the expansion of <term>Chesed|Kindness; the first emotional Sefirah</term>, as the Rabbis of blessed memory explained in the **Assembly** <note>original: "Idra," referring to the Idra Rabba or Idra Zuta sections of the Zohar</note>. At the time of his passing—and therefore *Yesod* and *Chesed* are entirely one matter. Likewise, we find in another place that the union of the <term>Malchut|Kingship; the feminine divine Presence</term> with <term>Tiferet|Beauty; the central masculine Sefirah</term> occurs through *Chesed*, as it is written regarding the aspect of *Yesod*... and his presence shall be anchored. "And turn your face here," etc., in the aspect of "and unto you we are joined." # The Dual Atonement: The Bull and the Scapegoat

They shall sweeten the judgment through the Scapegoat <note>Hebrew: *Sa’ir*, the goat sent to Azazel</note> which was [associated with] his wife and this, and all his sin. They did not distinguish a portion from them.

They ascended, and the argument was in his hand against his brother, the High Priest, regarding kindness. They shall be merited from the city; a good sin-offering is made, and this is made a sin-offering. The one who awakens [mercy] knows that the whole city did not know the service of all the Priests. These are necessary for the Holy Temple. It is known that the "weeks" <note>likely referring to the priestly shifts or "Mishmarot"</note> obligated the offspring who remain, as they were mentioned for the benefit of their lives—they are poor and we are unable to do good for them.

The [laying of] hands shall be upon the Scapegoat. Grace was given to him, and power—how is this for them? ## The Justification for Seeking Divine Wisdom

<meta>Continuity: Following the previous page’s discussion on the "Peace of the Kingdom" and the ascent through the spiritual worlds, this page provides a foundational explanation of the Ten Sefirot (Divine emanations). And these <term>Ten Sefirot<note>Hebrew: *Eser Sefirot*; the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite interacts with the universe.</note></term>, <term>as it were<note>original: *k’veyachol*; a traditional qualifier used when describing God in human terms to emphasize that these are only metaphors.</note></term>, are the powers of man and his limbs. Just as the intellect and the human body are divided into three primary parts—<term>CHaBaD<note>Acronym for *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), *Binah* (Understanding), and *Da’at* (Knowledge).</note></term>, <term>CHaGaT<note>Acronym for *Chesed* (Kindness), *Gevurah* (Might), and *Tiferet* (Beauty).</note></term>, and <term>NeHiYM<note>Acronym for *Netzach* (Victory), *Hod* (Splendor), *Yesod* (Foundation), and *Malchut* (Kingship/Sovereignty).</note></term>—so too are the Ten Sefirot. Three are the intellect, called Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge; their place is in the brain of the head, and from them emerge thought and comprehension. They are the governors of all the limbs and fill them with life and power. Three are Kindness, Might, and Beauty; they are the instruments of deed and action, and they correspond to the parts of the body: the right arm, the left arm, and the body itself. Three are Victory, Splendor, and Foundation; they are the instruments of movement, walking, and procreation, and they are in the right thigh, the left thigh, and the reproductive organ.

And these Ten Sefirot are His Emanation, blessed be He, and they are divided in this world into ten levels of intellect, power, and soul. They are the aspect of the "Man of Emanation" <note>Hebrew: *Adam d'Atzilut*; the highest spiritual structure of the Divine attributes in the shape of a human.</note> who illuminates all the other worlds: the <term>World of Creation<note>Hebrew: *Olam HaBriah*.</note></term>, the <term>World of Formation<note>Hebrew: *Olam HaYetzirah*.</note></term>, and the <term>World of Action<note>Hebrew: *Olam HaAsiyah*.</note></term>. These are the Ten Sefirot of Emanation, referred to as "the Points," each one comprised of ten, and in their totality they are one hundred. Likewise, the Ten Sefirot of Creation, the Ten Sefirot of Formation, and the Ten Sefirot of Action each have the likeness of a man, possessing limbs in the brain, arms, and thighs.

As for what you asked—whether the Ten Sefirot are ten levels one above the other like a ladder standing on the ground with its top reaching the heavens—know that this is not the case. Rather, they are circular, one within the other like <term>onion skins<note>original: *galdei betzalim*; a classic Kabbalistic metaphor for the nested nature of spiritual realities.</note></term>, just as the celestial spheres are circular, one within the other. Each one of them includes ten Sefirot, and they are called Emanation, Creation, Formation, and Action. The order of the Ten Sefirot in each of these worlds is: Wisdom, Understanding, Knowledge, Kindness, Might, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Kingship. Wisdom is the "brain" of the head; it is the first point and the root of all wisdoms. It is His wisdom, blessed be He, which can neither be grasped nor known. And Understanding is...

<column-break/>

And Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge, which are in the brain of the head: Wisdom is the power that brings something into existence from nothingness; Understanding is that which understands one thing from within another thing; and Knowledge is that which decides between them and is established in the soul. These are a metaphor for the Supernal Ten Sefirot which are His Emanation, blessed be He. From them were emanated the Ten Sefirot of Creation, the Ten Sefirot of Formation, and the Ten Sefirot of Action. All of them are in the likeness of a man, called the Man of Creation, the Man of Formation, and the Man of Action. 

The order of these Ten Sefirot in every single world is as follows: Wisdom, Understanding, Knowledge, Kindness, Might, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Kingship. Behold, Wisdom is the first point, called "Holy," and it is the root of everything and the source of all wisdoms; it is His wisdom, blessed be He, which can neither be grasped nor known. Understanding is the "expanse" and the "building" in which all things emerging from Wisdom are detailed; it is the Understanding from which all paths are divided. Knowledge is the bond that connects Wisdom with Understanding; it is the aspect of the Soul that connects thought with speech, and it is the aspect of the pause and the connection between the intellect and action.

Kindness, Might, and Beauty are three attributes: Love, Fear, and Mercy. Just as they exist as attributes of the soul, so they are in the Supernal Sefirot: Kindness is Love, Might is Fear, and Beauty is the Mercy that decides between them. Victory, Splendor, and Foundation are the instruments of deed, action, and drawing down [divine flow]; they are the aspects of triumph, thanksgiving, and binding. And Kingship <note>Hebrew: *Malchut*.</note> is the recipient from all of them; she is called the <term>Assembly of Israel<note>Hebrew: *Knesset Yisrael*; in Kabbalah, this refers to the Sefirah of Malchut as the spiritual source of the Jewish people and the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) in the world.</note></term>, and she is the aspect of speech and lower governance. 

These Ten Sefirot are grasped one in the other and bound one to the other; there is no separation in them at all, God forbid, for all is one, like a <term>flame bound to a coal<note>A classic metaphor from the *Sefer Yetzirah* describing the unity of God and His attributes.</note></term>. A person must know that these Sefirot are the aspects of His governance, blessed be He, of His world; there is no change in them from His side, but only from the side of the recipients. Furthermore, one should know that these Ten Sefirot are divided into three columns: the Right Column, the Left Column, and the Middle Column. The Right Column consists of Wisdom, Kindness, and Victory. The Left Column consists of Understanding, Might, and Splendor. The Middle Column consists of Knowledge, Beauty, Foundation, and Kingship.

->Three stories are contained in the "Chapter of the Pious One," <note>Hebrew: *Perek de-Chasida*</note> and so it is found in the Midrash.<-

"And a foolish son is the grief of his mother," <note>Proverbs 10:1</note> for in these matters the dominion of the <term>Evil Inclination<note>Hebrew: *Yetzer Ha-Ra*; the innate human drive toward physical gratification or selfish desires, which can lead to sin if not mastered.</note></term> is made known—it is hidden in the heart of man, and such a person has no fear of the One who knows the secrets of the heart.

The first story is about a certain pious man who was occupied with the Torah and with great integrity. Once, a "bad spirit" <note>Likely referring to a state of deep depression or a psychological-spiritual ailment.</note> struck him, and from his great worry, he grew increasingly diminished until his strength weakened; he was unable to stand in prayer or perform good deeds. Regarding this, it is said in the *Book of Ethics* <note>Hebrew: *Sefer Ha-Musar*; a general term for Jewish ethical literature focused on character refinement.</note> that when a person sees their soul becoming lazy in the service of the Creator, blessed be He, they should consider that this stems from a "bad temperament" or a change in their <unclear>natural</unclear> constitution, and so on. We know he should strive with all his might to strengthen the body and remove that weakness; afterward, he will see if he can stand his ground and overcome the Inclination. He should reflect that if his thoughts were pure and clear, the Inclination would not have ruled over him.

The second story concerns a young man who was occupied with the Torah and was unattached. The Evil Inclination came upon him to make him stumble through wine and drunkenness. The Inclination overcame him until he sinned and caused others to sin. When he felt in his soul that he had erred in this, he regretted it with a complete <term>repentance<note>Hebrew: *Teshuvah*; literally "return," the process of atonement and spiritual realignment with God.</note></term>. He took it upon himself to perform great <term>asceticism<note>Hebrew: *Siguf*; self-affliction or fasting intended to atone for sins and subdue the physical body.</note></term> and wept bitterly in his soul until his prayer reached the heavens. They forgave him from Heaven, and it became clear that he had merited that high level. Repentance is an exalted virtue that transforms the countenance, and it is never nullified unless a person darkens their soul with a <term>willful sin<note>Hebrew: *Zadon*; a sin committed intentionally and with full knowledge, rather than by accident.</note></term>. Regarding this, it is said in the Midrash: "Let Dan judge his people as one" <note>Genesis 49:16</note> and "How great are your works, O Lord" <note>Psalms 104:24</note>. All of man’s toil is external, <unclear>and a thorn</unclear> in the Midrash states: "All of man's toil is for his mouth." <note>Ecclesiastes 6:7</note> Remember that the honorable person enjoys the <term>Radiance of the Divine Presence<note>Hebrew: *Ziv Ha-Shekhinah*; the spiritual light or delight experienced by the soul in the proximity of God.</note></term>, while the body, being lower, enjoys natural foods. When a person habituates their body to the pleasures of this world, they diminish the enjoyment of the soul—especially when committing a transgression that leads to the neglect of a <unclear>positive</unclear> commandment.

Repentance and asceticism, and the matter of the "Stone of the Wise": Behold, one must be strong against the Evil Inclination, which has five "daughters": Envy, Physical Lust, Pride, Covetousness, and Hatred. The third story is about a young man who was occupied with the Torah and was very poor. He used to sell straw and hay. His companion came and said to him, "How long will you live in this distress?" He replied, "What can I do? Such is the decree of the Omnipresent." His companion said, "Why do you not switch to another trade that yields much profit, namely, selling spices?" He replied, "I have no money to buy the merchandise." His companion said, "I will lend to you; buy spices from me and take them to other places to sell." He did so, and when he saw that the business was going well, his heart became proud. He set his eyes on another woman and was with her at the bathhouse, and a "bad spirit" struck him. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Anyone who leaves his worthy wife and goes to another is as if he serves idols and denies the Root <note>original: *Kafar b'Ikkar*; to deny the fundamental existence or unity of God.</note>." Concerning this, it is said in the *Book of Ethics* that the Inclination will entice a person until he sins, and afterward, it ascends on high to prosecute him.

Behold, when this man felt his illness, he repented and gave all his money to the poor, built a synagogue, and fasted for many days because of this sin. They sent healing from Heaven and he was cured. Regarding this, it is said: "As the size of the sin, so shall be the size of the repentance." The essence of repentance is what atones for the sin, and afterward, the person will be clean of his sin. Even though he was healed, he was not as strong as he was at first; he conducted himself with great <term>abstinence<note>Hebrew: *Perishut*; a life of self-restraint and withdrawal from physical pleasures for spiritual purposes.</note></term> until the day of his death. Behold, all these stories come to teach how great is the power of Repentance, which reaches even to the Throne of Glory. It is proper for every person to be careful in their soul against every stumbling block and matter of <term>immorality<note>Hebrew: *Ervah*; literally "nakedness," referring to forbidden sexual relations.</note></term>, so that they may not have an "opening of the mouth" <note>i.e., a reason to be condemned or a lack of defense.</note> when appearing before the Heavenly Court in the time [to come].

### The Emergence of the Chariot and Divine Thought

To weave together the powers of the <term>Merkavah<note>Hebrew: *Merkavah*; the "Divine Chariot" or the structure of the celestial realms as envisioned by the prophet Ezekiel.</note></term> from among them, He blends them so they may emerge; from them, they are transformed into every aspect and detail. You will see that the diverse heavenly lights emerge from a single source. This is the meaning of the phrase:
->**"Awesome in praises"**<- <note>Exodus 15:11: "Who is like You, majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, doing wonders?"</note>
What does "Awesome in praises" signify? Since they are divided into "Front" and "Back" <note>An allusion to the different ways Divine light is perceived: directly (Front) or through hiddenness and reflection (Back).</note>, it becomes "Awesome," for there is no aspect that is not part of the One; this is why He can have "praises." Likewise, consider the "might of Your hands." In the aspect where they are "Front" and where they are "Back," they are unified with the Divine Name.

The Holy One, blessed be He, hinted at that **Thought** within this very Thought, and through it, everything came into being. With a subtle gesture, He called it "Holy." This is known from the concept of the **Addition to the Sabbath** <note>Hebrew: *Tosefet Shabbat* — the practice of starting the Sabbath early, pulling the holiness of the seventh day into the sixth.</note>, which begins before the actual seventh day starts. Through this, all worlds are elevated to the light of the **Crown** (*Keter*), which is the supernal holiness where the light of the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) dwells. The concept of the **Extra Soul** <note>Hebrew: *Neshamah Yeteirah* — the additional spiritual dimension granted to every Jew during the Sabbath.</note> on the Sabbath is a foretaste of this high level. It is this soul that descends and clothes itself in the human body, granting it an exalted spiritual power. The supernal union and "coupling" of the Sabbath day is what draws down all blessings and spiritual influences to the six days of the work week. This is what is written: "For on it He rested from all His work which God created to do."

# Introduction

->Introduction<-

The word "Speech" refers to the attainment of governance, which is the joining together of Thought, Speech, and Action. This is well known from the *Book of Splendor* <note>original: "Sefer HaZohar," the foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> regarding the verse describing a <unclear>heavy</unclear> <unclear>burden</unclear> that weighs <unclear>upon me</unclear> through thought, speech, and action. 
What is the matter of the trials and the <unclear>souls</unclear> <unclear>as if</unclear> <unclear>when</unclear> <unclear>they</unclear> <unclear>are</unclear> <unclear>within</unclear> <unclear>the power</unclear> of thought? Thought alone is not considered <unclear>an action</unclear>.
There are two Names and a distinction in their workings: the Lord God <note>original: "YHWH Elohim"</note>, for in each of them He is Creator, Former, and Maker.

<meta>This page transitions from a discussion of mystical Sefirot to a reconciliation of traditional Jewish cosmology with the "new" Copernican astronomy. It cites the Talmud (Pesachim 94b) and biblical passages (Joshua and Habakkuk) to argue that even the ancient Sages recognized the validity of alternative astronomical models.</meta>

And this matter occurred in our commentary on the verse: "Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens" <note>original: "Hen l'Adonai Elohekha ha-shamayim" (Deuteronomy 10:14)</note>. From here, let us return and state that the early Sages of Israel, of blessed memory, were very proficient in the matter of the heavens and the rotation of the spheres of the stars. The sages of the Greeks, who came after them, reached the same opinion and agreement, even though they differed on a minor matter as mentioned in the book of the Gemara, from Tractate Pesachim, in the eighth chapter: <note>Though the text cites Chapter 8, this famous discussion is found in the 9th chapter of Pesachim, 94b.</note>

> For the Sages of Israel say: By day the sun travels below the firmament, and by night it rises above the firmament. But the sages of the nations of the world say: By day the sun travels below the firmament, and by night below the earth. And this matter is a subject of explicit dispute there in the aforementioned chapter, and this is the language of the aforementioned Gemara:
> Our Rabbis taught: The Sages of Israel say the sphere is fixed and the constellations revolve, while the sages of the nations of the world say the sphere revolves and the constellations are fixed. Rabbi [Judah the Prince] said: A refutation to their words [the Sages of Israel] is that we have never found the Great Bear in the south or Scorpio in the north. Rabbi Aha bar Yaakov said etc. And Rabbi Judah the Prince, who lived at that time, heard the words of the sages of the nations of the world and agreed with them, saying: "Their words appear more correct than ours, for by day the springs are cool, and by night they are boiling." <note>This refers to the ancient belief that if the sun traveled beneath the Earth at night, it would heat the subterranean waters.</note>

And so we have come to the opinion of the sages of the nations of the world, that the heavens revolve around all the earth, all around. This is the intent of the scripture "the wheel of the heavens." The matter of prophecy regarding this subject has already been explained in the previous verse in the Book of Scriptures, and it is most explicit in the Book of Joshua: "And the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day" <note>Joshua 10:13</note>. This matter refers to the sun standing in the middle of the sky at midday, and it "hasted not to go down about a whole day"—meaning that all the travel it would usually perform in a full day, it performed while standing still for that one day. This is why the scripture says "it stood in the midst of heaven." And if we return and ask on which day it stood, we can explicitly say it was the day of the Summer Solstice <note>original: "Tekufat Tammuz," the summer season/solstice</note> when it stood in the midst of heaven, for by its nature throughout the year, this is the highest of all days. When it stood there on that day, it was seen to be at its height. All this was a great and revealed miracle. This statement we made regarding this verse, "The sun stood still etc.," adds to our explanation of the verse "The moon stood in its habitation" <note>Habakkuk 3:11</note>, which is the second prophecy we arrive at from the Book of Habakkuk. From the explanation of this scripture, the prophet Habakkuk said that the moon and the sun stood in a high place. In this, the prophet revealed the matter to us in a hidden way, saying: "Moon and sun stood in Zevul." The meaning of "Zevul" is the high height of the heavens, because Zevul is an upper place. Likewise, our Sages of blessed memory said there are seven heavens, and Zevul is the <unclear>fourth</unclear> <unclear>according to the Midrash</unclear> <unclear>found</unclear> <unclear>in the</unclear> <unclear>aforementioned chapter</unclear> <unclear>and belt</unclear>.

<column-break/>

He remembered and turned a stormy wind. # In the Beginning

Portions of the words of Torah are portions of the "Conduct" <note>original: "Hanhaga," Divine governance</note>, and this conduct is the Speech that is illuminated within this speech, and in the words of our Sages of blessed memory, and in Understanding. The commentators have placed it in its proper position. The unique attribute is worthy: "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth" <note>Genesis 1:1</note> through Wisdom <note>original: "Chochmah"</note>. It is Wisdom through which the name *Ehyeh* <note>original: "I Will Be," the name of God revealed at the Burning Bush</note> appeared; it illuminates everything, and all the luminaries are planted within it. Behold the Great and Unique Name, the Name called "Beginning of Speech," and in it the attribute is established. It is called the "Secret of Simplicity," and it is the general gateway of Wisdom and the gateway of the heart, called "Beginning" <note>original: "Bereishit"</note>. Concerning this attribute, the scripture says: "For with Your wisdom I shall be..."

->And the Supreme God made for him the entrance with a gate of gold.<-

**The Crown** <note>original: "Keter," the highest Sefirah</note> is the head of all existences, the Ancient One which is the source and foundation in the "womb." Within it are the heavens, and within them, the letters used for their foundation were mixed. There is a hint within them that they are a Throne and canopies from the earth. In the name of the Lord <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> the letters of His arrangement are hinted at, the path that ascends to it, and with it, perhaps they shall be revealed.

**Wisdom** <note>original: "Chochmah"</note> is the clear, white, and explicit Thought; it is not hinted at in writing or by relation. Within the Thought, one may not ask "Why?" Within it, the witnesses and security are known, as is the "Silver." Wisdom is dependent upon Understanding, and within it, the "Before" provides weight and skill.

**Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"</note> is the power in which speech is materialized. Within it are the "Hidden Words" that emerge to the "Wall." It is engaged in Torah and the most excellent labor, for prayer is in the secret of Speech on the practical path.

**Kindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note> is that which is considered in the heart and pours out ethical instruction <note>original: "Musar"</note> to bring it into action. It is the "Strong Hand" and the "Mighty Hand" under which one takes refuge in the God of Kindness on the day He stands. Kindness is called His "Right Hand," and "from His right hand, a fiery law of kindness" <note>a play on Deuteronomy 33:2</note> comes to us through our Shepherd, Abraham, representing ethical instruction and continuity. Within the Hand of Kindness, Judgment <note>Din</note> is thickened, and from it comes ethical discipline.

**Fear** <note>original: "Pachad," another name for Gevurah/Might</note> is that which stands in the "Watch of the Place." Upon it is the Might <note>Gevurah</note> that ascends through the thick part of the Conduct of the world. It is written: "Awesome in His standing." For all existences, trembling is visible from the Name, and all created beings shall fear the strength of Might. This is Fear, in which the most excellent Commandment resides; this is the Dreaded Power, and from this, the Patriarchs acquired this commandment.

**Beauty** <note>original: "Tiferet"</note> is that in which the Name placed the Sun to bring out the luminary into the day. In this secret, it is stretched out and understanding. This is the attribute that interweaves the "six ends" within it. Just as the Name dwells within the Holy Temple and within the heavens, so too regarding this attribute is it written: "And You shall hear from the heavens." This attribute is what speaks in the name of the Ascending Luminary, and it is supreme in the name of the Shining Luminary, above all the precious and great names; for this Name is unique to them, and through them His name is known, and it is the Honored Name.

**Victory** <note>original: "Netzach"</note> is the power that stands in this attribute and the great power of the victory of the world.
**Splendor** <note>original: "Hod"</note> is the attribute joined with it, together with these, and it is the capacity within it.

<meta>This page continues the technical exploration of the Divine names and the creative process, specifically how Wisdom (Chokhmah) manifests through the Hebrew alphabet and the structures described in the Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Formation). Through this, the words of the Sage, of blessed memory, will be explained—that we are compelled to recognize Him by virtue of His standing at the height of the world, and so on. 
The **Holy Wisdom** <note>original: "HaChokhmah HaKedoshah"</note> states: "The matters shall be clarified further through testimony, and all the more so if you merit to understand..." etc., regarding the changing of the Names. With this, the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "Sefer Yetzirah," the foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note> shall be fulfilled in the "Eternal House." 

The reason for this matter is that a word does not actually emerge from a person's mouth until it exists potentially within the soul. When the time for its emergence arrives, the soul returns to it and gives it life. This is the explanation of what we mentioned: that the name of a "word" is found in its letters, and afterward, He "decreed" <note>or carved</note> the letters, and the second "split" them, and so on.

Likewise, the power of the changing letters—which is drawn from **Wisdom**—does not exist without the Divine. The essences were not gathered or decreed until afterward, when He added to them. This is the concept of the "second" and the "cutting." For instance, He took "Adam" <note>Man</note> and removed the letter *Aleph*, placing a *Vav* in its stead... <note>This likely refers to a mystical permutation of the name of Man</note>.

This is the indwelling of the **Divine Presence** <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> upon the Holy. Afterward, it was divided into forty-two <note>referring to the 42-letter Name of God</note> and changed.

It is not that He changed, God forbid, but rather that these forces spread into these places, and the Name is mentioned according to the capacity of the receiver. As the Sage said: "Do not wonder if the Name changes in all places in its letters." Even though this thing is difficult—that it should be "good" at one time and different at another—the Sages said of the Name that He is "Mercy" and a "Merciful Judge," truly showing mercy and truly judging the wicked. Because He was Mercy, His judgment was also truly merciful, yet the "mercy of the sinner" is nothing, for His mercy and judgment are toward His Will, not from a human perspective. 

Even when God perceived those He created on the earth and the human being in two aspects, there is a difference found in the *Books of Formation*. In the **Ashkenaz version** <note>The German/European manuscript tradition of this mystical text</note>, we see it as pure and clear, unchanging, with no "profanation of the Names," God forbid. In every language, I shall provide the Names. 

According to this, the place of those [forces] shall be explained, as well as the "poured wine" of the receiver. For the light of the sun is nothing other than a reflection of "Good and Good." Because the Name desired the luminaries, here is **Wisdom**, of blessed memory; even though these are words of truth, this suffices.

# The Nature of Divine Perfection and the Soul

And behold, according to the estimation of the perfection of the matter before the Holy One, blessed be He, this is the depth of what is commonly said: for the matter of the "length of days" <note>original: *Arichat Hayamim*; often referring to the divine attribute of Mercy or long life</note> and the "depths," and each of them is a power for the service of the Name <note>original: *Hashem*; a common way to refer to G-d</note> according to its value. According to the **Revealed** and the **Hidden** <note>original: *Nigleh* and *Nistar*; the dual nature of Torah study</note>, they are as mentioned above. Afterward, he will clarify a proper matter in the explanation of the word "Hidden"—a thing that is concealed <unclear>according to</unclear> when investigation and mystery come. Behold, the revealed portion and the complete portion in terms of the **Soul** and the **Body** are both <unclear>attached</unclear>. Just as the soul is known to be within the body, like the matter of the breath of life within the frame. In the Book of Joshua, it is said that the "Gilgal" <note>original: *Ha-Gilgal*; referring to the site of the first encampment in Israel, meaning "circle" or "rolling away"</note> was <unclear>to open</unclear> to the simple, and further on these are the famous attributes: "The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble." He brings the aspect of the **Eighteen Foundations** <note>original: *Yod-Chet Yesod*; likely referring to the eighteen blessings of the central prayer, the Amidah</note> and the deep thought within this; the one of small understanding will grasp a little. He spoke a very deep matter due to its nature, for I shall store the foundation of **Metatron** <note>original: *MT"T*; the primary angel in kabbalistic literature who serves as the heavenly scribe</note>, in whom is the power of breaking and destruction from the matter of "on the day of the sword." This is what is called by the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, for truly all seven days of the week are found in the **Tikkunei Zohar** <note>A fundamental kabbalistic text focusing on the 70 repairs/explanations of the first word of Genesis</note>. # The Emanation of the Ten Sefirot

And indeed, after the explanation of the matter of the expansion of the **Ten Sefirot** <note>The ten divine attributes or channels of emanation</note> from the **Crown** <note>original: *Keter*; the highest Sefirah</note> has been clarified—how they are immersed within it and the Crown is within them, and likewise in all of them <unclear>in the aspect of the internal</unclear>—the Master <note>the Arizal</note> of blessed memory wrote that in this is a complete explanation. Behold, it is found that in the portion of the "Water" in the river that descended below, there is within them the aspect of the **Simple Waters** of the **Infinite** <note>original: *Ein Sof*; the unknowable G-d prior to emanation</note> deep within them, as mentioned above in the explanation of the matter of the Water. Even though they are "adjacent and visible," nevertheless these waters are in the aspect of the **Soul**, and they are guarded with a supreme guarding in the aspect of the **Body**. For the part of it that remains below is the aspect of the body and the vitality, which is **Sovereignty** <note>original: *Malchut*; the lowest Sefirah, associated with the physical world</note>. However, the aspect of holiness and the height that is deep within it is called "Place" and "Boundary" from the outside. The wise one who understands the complete matter and the degree of the depth of thought knows that it is one domain and <unclear>place</unclear>. There is a verse: "Beloved are Israel, for they are called Children of the Place" <note>A quote from Pirkei Avot; "The Place" (*HaMakom*) is a name for G-d</note>, for the soul is the aspect of the "Understander." For it is the secret of the **Engraving of Thought**. Here we have found an indication regarding the matter of Thought, the supreme Form, the acronym of: "And G-d said, Let there be light" <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. For these are the sublime lights through which the world was created. The light is called "Day," as said regarding the matter of the Holy and Sublime Repair, which is called the **Outer Palace of the King**. The light is not like a document to the world; it is my light, and all the Sefirot were influenced by its prophecy. Our Comforter is one and unique; He is the Creator, the Fashioner, and the Influencer. For the purpose of the **Union** in the manner of deep, intensified prophecy is that the Holy Intellect is above the "Object of Intellect" and its grasp. It is a world-form of light, and it is the **Upper Union**, and it is called the "Form of Essence," and its grasp is in Thought. This is the secret of **Knowledge** (*Da'at*). Behold, this is what will be the search of the general **Lower Union** of the secret of the attachment and seal of the matter of **Blessing** and **Holiness** that is acted upon and the emotional movement of the <unclear>world</unclear>. Two Gates exist in the part of Thought for man. For it is the matter of the Exalted Union, the aspect of the Soul that hastens through all the letters of the Torah. They are in the aspect of what the Sages of blessed memory said: after they gave him permission to use the **Tablets** <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, they gave him Wisdom and Understanding. For he understands through the "Judaism of the Brain." Behold, when a man enters into this deep thought, it is the Intellect called the **Spring** which flows and draws down. They stood in the body and did not separate from it for even a moment; it was like the connection of the soul and the body as mentioned. And so in the Scripture, it is almost the same matter in which every matter is sealed in the secret of "Nickname" and "Imagination." The student should examine these words very carefully—the matter of the essence in the aspect of the intellect—so that he does not distance the Union from his thought, as mentioned in the **Tikkunei Zohar**. The student will understand this like the "fish of the sea" <note>A metaphor for being surrounded by the divine presence as fish are surrounded by water</note>.

# The Nature of Prophecy and the Return of the Divine Presence

To everyone, he pressed according to their ability. Behold, all of this was hinted at by the King-Angel in the word he taught the prophet at that hour.

# The Fifty Gates and the Ascent of the Soul

Among the **Beholders** <note>original: *Nevatim*; likely referring to those with prophetic vision or "sprouts" of wisdom</note>, behold, on the fiftieth day, within the secret of my soul, it is written regarding **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*; the third Sefirah, associated with the divine mother and the expansion of thought</note> and God: **Fifty Gates of Understanding** were created in the world, and all but one were given to Moses <note>A classic Talmudic statement from Tractate Nedarim 38a regarding the limits of human comprehension</note>, as is found in the **Zohar** <note>The primary work of Jewish mysticism</note>, the Midrashim, and the **Later Sages** <note>original: *Achronim*; rabbinic authorities from the 16th century to the present</note. This is the "river issuing from Eden," and Moses merited to cross it through every doubt and absence. These occurrences are spoken of through the kindness of the Name [God]. Therefore, it is called a "river," as mentioned in the aforementioned *Likutei Or* <note>"Gathered Lights," likely a specific mystical text</note>. By the consensus of the supernal thoughts, the matter is clear: the "Son of the Prophet" is the foundation of the secret regarding life—they are the collective. The sign of this is that Man (*Adam*) is first "Life," possessing the foundation of **Knowledge** <note>original: *Da'at*</note>, which extends into time.

The matter of thought and Divine Providence knows the state of "Man as a sinner," specifically in the details of things. This is the level from this height called "Man" (*Adam*), who merited to attain the truth of the **Holy Soul** <note>original: *Neshama*</note>. For the measure is not a "spider" <note>likely a metaphor for fragility or insignificance</note>, but rather Understanding; the relationship of a man to his soul is like the cloud-like height above the physical. He [the person] is **Wisdom** <note>original: *Chokhmah*</note> who merited the Heavens, for his deeds on earth are "Judgment," "Man," and "Form." This resides within the known soul and the **Divine Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>, which is Life. There is a sense of the **Lower Soul** <note>original: *Nefesh*</note>, which is the Sabbath and the "Name of Life."

So, by His kindness at this time, "I shall be" <note>original: *Ehyeh*; a Divine Name associated with Keter or Binah</note> like this—possessing an intrinsic nature in the aspect of Man, so that he may be a Man of goodness, truth, and holy perfection. After he had lived in a "year of falsehood," he proved it through a *fortiori* argument <note>original: *Kal Vachomer*; a logical inference from a minor premise to a major one</note>. The foundation of the world is **Peace**, and therefore it shall be considered etc. This is like the living creatures [angels]... these things are in the introduction, for they are great principles in that Book of Books. In them are faith, truth, and kindness—or the love of money, for through money one fixes the "fruit" that was. See this matter regarding the righteousness of souls, the Torah, and Prayer. Their removal is not humility, but intended to sweeten the souls. Because we shall "count the [days]" and the "shofar blast" <note>original: *Teruah*</note> for this. The heart knows what is good and what is not truth; may it rise for [divine] favor and be considered. They shall know and wonder at the Holy One, Blessed be He, regarding the matter of "examination" and the secret of **Repentance** <note>original: *Teshuvah*</note>, along with the **humble Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinah aluvah*</note>. The intention of the heart is joined with the words; their meaning is that a word of truth was in Man, and he toiled, and all the "power of good" in the world and tranquility [were his]. This is the tranquility of our happiness among the bad [times], for today they have fallen. By His blessed intellect, "Israel shall rejoice" in the choice of rest, as our God the King ascended to the dwelling of the festival of **Beholders** in life, truth, and kindness—the word of a wise man.

<column-break/>

He has the judgment of a **Prince** <note>original: *Nasi*; a leader or communal head</note> in the sense of "behold, the dwelling of a Prince." This is hinted at in the Torah portion of **Yitro** <note>Jethro, Moses' father-in-law</note>. It comes to teach us about the **Convert** <note>original: *Ger*; referring to Jethro as a righteous proselyte</note>. He is within the Wisdom called "Yitro," for the name *Yitro* comes from the language of **Advantage** <note>original: *Yitron*; a surplus or excellence</note>. That is to say, an extra portion of the soul was added to him, an advantage over the "crude soul" within him. When he prepared himself with the other parts of the soul, the "Designated Soul" entered him. Through this, he merited to ascend and inherit all the good traits, the attributes, the strength, and all greatness. He merited to ascend and cleave to the **Heavenly Academy** <note>original: *Yeshivah shel Ma'alah*</note>. It is said of him, "it was pleasant for him to contemplate" when he took hold of the Academy that he ascended to. He sits in truth, even though they told him, "This is not your place," for this is the man who takes hold of the "teeth" <note>levels or segments</note> of the two parts of Wisdom. This is the **Beholder** that [the sage] mentions at the end of his words: in the time of exile and concealment, when his service is not visible to the eye—even if he is at the level of "Strength" and "Beholding" above the aforementioned stage—he is not called a "distinguished wise man," even if he is wise. This is according to our opinion and the words of the [sages]. It is even better that the secrets of the "Words of Life" [be hidden].

In our time, **Elijah** <note>the Prophet</note> was sanctified and merited prophecy. And when they knew that the soul of **Rabbi Joshua ben Levi** <note>A 3rd-century sage known in legends for entering Paradise alive</note> was called the "Four-fold Chariot" <note>original: *Merkavah Arba*; referring to the Divine Chariot in Ezekiel's vision</note>, for the Holy One is called Wisdom, the Chariot of this [level]. He [God] gave him prophecy, and he served in the **Holy Temple** <note>original: *Beit Ha-Mikdash*</note>. Every Sabbath... the great [Academy] called "Peace" among the creatures, even the gentiles, and especially among his own kind. He merited and was given a precious portion also in a high degree, even stronger, called the "Ancient" in the aspect of the "Upper Beholding" of the Four-fold Chariot. For in seven levels... and all that is proper within him... and behold, in his consolation from the levels, there is the **Source of the Chariot**. All the rest and their foundations are the "Upper One of the Upper Wisdom" which support the fulfillment of the commandments for all the "appointed times of the attributes."

His "Good Memory" <note>referring to a deceased righteous person</note> transforms the [letter] *Vav*, for this is also high. For this, the **Tannaim** <note>Sages of the Mishnah</note> came in other statements and were mentioned in the Synagogues, which are in the aspect of Wisdom and their "Sign." The soul of **Enoch** <note>The biblical figure who "walked with God" and was transformed into the angel Metatron</note>, who is called *Chanoch*, merited that in the aspect of the "Supernal Man" <note>original: *Adam Ha-Elyon*</note> called "Man," he dwelt in joy and gladness, as it is written: *“And Enoch walked with God, and he was no more, for God took him”* [Genesis 5:24]. He was taken above the [usual] level, for that is **Eternity** <note>original: *Netzach*; the seventh Sefirah, associated with victory and endurance</note> in the level of the **Divine Presence**, as mentioned above. Some say that he completed the [measure of] eight in the merit of the **Beholders**. And who is it that upholds the "Chronicles"? He who engages in the **Secret Torah** <note>original: *Torah Ha-Nistarah*; Kabbalah</note>, even the "Secret" mentioned in the previous chapter. The matter placed within the generation is called the "Path of Peace," of which it is written: **Peace**, and no man harms him. Therefore, he is called **Pious** <note>original: *Chasid*</note> and **Wise**.

### 28

And so it is said: *And He was grieved in His heart* <note>Genesis 6:6; usually interpreted as God's reaction to the wickedness of the generation of the Flood</note>. <meta>This page continues the philosophical and mystical exploration of the Covenant, moving from the symbolic "Rainbow" discussed previously to the relationship between physical action and the Divine Intellect. It builds on the idea that human conduct must align with the "straight conduct" of the upper realms.</meta>

For the **practical commandments** <note>original: *mitzvot ma’asiyot*</note> are to the intellect like a servant is to his master, or like a craftsman’s tool in the house of a master-craftsman. The tool does not understand the custom or the will of the master, but only the function of the instruments—such as the press, the saw, or the oven. Regarding these, it is said that the **commandments between man and God** <note>original: *bein adam la-makom*</note> have no "rational taste" <note>Meaning they lack a self-evident logical reason.</note>; they exist only to habituate a person to the will of the **Cause of Causes** (blessed be He) and to awaken the intellect within them to read the Torah portions that establish counsel in His name (may He be exalted). These are the practical commandments known as **traditional commandments** <note>original: *mitzvot shemiyot*, literally "auditory commandments" received through tradition rather than derived by reason.</note>, meaning they are accepted from the Torah. Through them, we understand how a person is awakened toward the intellect and the words of the Prophet regarding these matters. This prophetic counsel involves five matters that were seen in the Second Temple. The general point of these preceding stories is **Kindness** <note>original: *Chesed*</note>, the sayings of the righteous; they are the beings called **Emanated Intellects**, by which I mean the **Ten Universal Spheres** <note>original: *eser sefirot olamiyot*</note> spoken of in the world of **Emanation** <note>original: *Atzilut*</note>. This is the meaning of: *And the Lord shall be one on that day, and His name One* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>, and everything shall exist in one awe and one dominion.

->In the first category and one part.<-

This continues with the usage of the prophetic theme and the awakening of the **Divine Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> within **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*</note> and **Mercy**. This refers to the Prophet Hezekiah and also the Prophet Isaiah, as well as Jerusalem, of which it is said: *And you shall be called "My Delight is in Her" and "Married"* <note>Isaiah 62:4</note>.

There is also the matter of the "Great Gate" and "Joseph," and the rest who shall be a prophet for Him. It says, "and the daughters of their divisions," corresponding to the measure of the lambs and the goat that were uprooted and overturned by the change in leadership that we see—a change corresponding to the measure of what is influenced. This is the "Supreme Custom" in its renewal, where they shall be "Face to Face" in faith. This "Heart" is linked to **Understanding** (*Binah*), and they said these are nothing but words of prophecy spoken at the slaughterhouse of the Holy Temple. When he says "the Altar of Burnt Offering," it is like the matter of the Altar of Burnt Offering which was the "Altar of Heaven." However, let every custom of the receiver with the *Shekhinah* be according to the measure of what is known from the custom of the "decree of His hands." This connection with the Lord is now well-explained, and how it was that this knowledge of the "custom of the receiver" was considered "bad" <note>Likely referring to the subjective human perception of divine judgment as "bad" or "evil."</note>. The intent behind the renewals of this custom is to be favorable, and from it, they derive the "taste" of the commandments. By the power of this custom, the healing of the *Shekhinah* is achieved.

<column-break/>

One matter follows another: we judge based on **corporeality** <note>original: *hagshamat*, the attribution of physical traits to God.</note>, and the Lord shall be in one of them besides what follows. There is the "mark of man" and other things that are not truly appropriate for them, such as the **Attributes** which are well-known. These are used as a **parable** <note>original: *mashal*</note> for the Leader who acts without chance or a change of will. We see this in the "Correction of the World," where He was "zealous" for the Patriarchs of the world; when He called out, He marked "zeal," and likewise "anger" and "wrath" and others in this way. Behold, this stands within itself: for the Lord, the Intellect, the Known, and the Knower are all one matter. To this, he hinted: "Kindness is an eternal world," if not for the benefit of the world of **Raphael**. Likewise, with the **Beauty of the World** <note>original: *Tiferet Olam*</note>, which are called "worlds." This is also said regarding the soul, to write "our eternal dwelling," and similarly regarding the "Creator of the Beginning" as "eternal," and many others like them.

By the power of this intellect, etc., and in the *Zohar* for the portion *Shemot* <note>Exodus</note>: it emerges from the Known Intellect and the Leader of the Will, the exalted and lofty. They also said in the *Songs of the Array* that this leadership is found with the **Infinite** <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note>, and it is the composition of the ten [Sefirot]. Three—which are **Understanding** (*Binah*), **Wisdom** (*Chochmah*), and the **Exalted Crown** (*Keter*)—are lofty and high within a single soul. All the rest—which are **Strength** (*Gevurah*), **Kindness** (*Chesed*), and **Mercy** (*Rachamim*)—and the three that follow them, are the Intellect, the Known, and the Knower. See the explanation of the words of the pious **Rabbi Isaac ibn Latif** <note>A 13th-century philosopher and Kabbalist who bridged the worlds of Maimonidean philosophy and early Kabbalah.</note> in his commentary on **Ecclesiastes** <note>original: *Kohelet*</note>, specifically the explanation of "the stones that divide" in this chapter. The general point of all this is to say that the Divine Speech never changes; rather, the change comes from the side of the **receivers**. This is like the example of an eye that is weak or pained when looking at the light of the sun: the light remains in its original state, but the pain is due to the weakness of the eye. This is the supreme counsel for why the practical commandments exist from the side of the Torah—for the sake of **straight conduct**. What the Prophet (of blessed memory) desired was to draw them toward the good, saying: *I do not desire the death of the one who dies... but that he turn from his way and live* <note>Ezekiel 18:32</note>. This is for the good of the world and its rest.

Behold, we have seen the trials performed for the Prophet <note>referring to Moses or Joshua</note>; if they were delayed, it was because of a lack of perfection. Behold, his intellect, his will, and their composition are like the matter our Sages (of blessed memory) mentioned: "Because one small thing was hidden from him." This was said to **Joshua**—and this matter of "Holy Joshua" is not appropriate for Joshua son of Nun <note>The author is likely distinguishing between the historical figure and a mystical archetype.</note>. This concerns the events mentioned at the end of the Book of Joshua, and the Sages mentioned these stories.

And these are the words of the Head of the Academy <note>original: *Rosh ha-Yeshiva*</note>, as well as those among the editors, regarding those who perform deeds in the name of **Action** <note>original: *Asiyah*; in Kabbalah, this refers to the physical world or the lowest of the four spiritual realms</note> and so on. This expression is for every person according to their freedom and their awakening, according to the poverty of their mind...

### The Camp
The **Interiority** is He, blessed be His Name, His light and His radiance; may it be the **Torah** <note>original: *Oraita*</note> and the light of the given brain. This is the "Clear Light." Rabbi Eliezer said regarding the reason of the soul: the explanation of the **Holy Light** is that it hovers, and from it the Kindness of Israel is destined to shine...

### The Crucible
This knowledge is the "pleasing aroma" from the Eternal to all worlds—the secret of perfection. For it is the movement of the **Superior Awakener**, the level of the Wisdom of the Hidden and Sanctified Glory. It is here, as it is said, "For it was and it went out" in the hidden Torah, the letters of the **Ancient Awakener** found in... And even if we take the words of our Sages of blessed memory, who measured this matter according to what is called **Action** <note>original: *Asiyah*</note>—such as when they tie parts of wool together—their intention was that the "craft" is done for that purpose. We shall now explain what has been clarified for us regarding the **Superior Soul**: that all the writings that transmit the "wounds of the blow"—of which it is said, "He who cleanses man from his sins"—in their explained names, refer to the **Kindness within Kindness** <note>original: *Chesed shebe-Chesed*</note> above. He spoke of the **Secret of Thought** given to them.

### 38

When the Sabbath of Hanukkah happens to fall on the **New Moon of Tevet** <term>Rosh Chodesh Tevet</term>, they take out three Torah scrolls. 
1. In the **first scroll**, the reader reads the weekly portion for six men. 
2. In the **second scroll**, he reads the portion for Hanukkah. 
3. On the second day, which is the ninth, they call seven men. 

On the seventh day, one reads the portion of the Menorah: "And this was the work of the Menorah" <note>Numbers 8:4</note>. In the third scroll, one reads about the eighth day of Hanukkah, regarding the offerings of the princes. On the eighth day and the sixth day, which is the New Moon, for the New Moon of Hanukkah, they use thirteen scrolls <note>This likely refers to the total scrolls used over the course of the week or a specific communal tradition</note>. After the New Moon, he reads in the second and the third from the Hanukkah portion and the Menorah portion, "This was the dedication of the Altar." They set aside the third scroll and return to read in the second the sacrifice of Hanukkah so that it completes the Hanukkah theme.

The "Lamp" is like the Sabbath. Such is the law when the New Moon falls on Thursday and Friday. On the Sabbath of Hanukkah, they take out three Torah scrolls: in one, they read for the New Moon with seven men; in the second, they read for Hanukkah; and in the third, "This was the dedication of the Altar," etc. 

On the Sabbath of the portion **Vayichi**, if Hanukkah falls within it, they read the **Haftarah** <term>the reading from the Prophets</term> "Sing and Rejoice" <note>Zechariah 2:14</note>. If it falls on the conclusion of the Sabbath of Hanukkah, they do not read the verses of *Vayichi*, but rather the Hanukkah Haftarah "Sing and Rejoice," as written in the **Prayer Book of the Ya’avetz** <note>Rabbi Jacob Emden (1697–1776), a leading rabbinic authority</note>; see there.

There is another custom among printers and proofreaders: the **Maftir** <term>the person who reads the concluding Torah portion and the Prophets</term> is from the Hanukkah portion, and from it he reads the Haftarah. In the place of Hanukkah, he brings out the New Moon scroll in the morning. Therefore, our Sages of blessed memory disagreed whether to read the Haftarah for the New Moon or for the Sabbath of Hanukkah. "Everything follows the local custom." 

The custom of these places is that they read for the New Moon, and likewise on the eighth lamp of Hanukkah, they read in one [scroll]. On the sixth, seventh, and eighth days, they read the portion of the Menorah: "And this was the Menorah." For they call seven men in the first scroll, and in the second he reads for Hanukkah. This is the correct way, so that the matter of Hanukkah is completed—all for Hanukkah—and that "This was the dedication of the Altar" is included. 

This beautiful custom was taken as a great ruling by the late Sage and proofreader in the section for printers. The book speaks of the Sabbath, Hanukkah, and the New Moon; then certainly one should call seven men for the New Moon portion, and in the second scroll read for Hanukkah on the sixth day, and in the third scroll read for the eighth day, "This was the dedication of the Altar." This is the correct way, Amen and Amen. 

Some Hanukkah books print "And Rabbi Hanukkah said" and "This is the Menorah," but do not mention the seventh and eighth days. The master printer told them the custom is good: on the days of the New Moon, in the second scroll, he reads for Hanukkah on the seventh day. Similarly in the **Mahzorim** <term>festival prayer books</term> and books of customs, they read on the seventh, eighth, and sixth days. I have heard this means they are required to read from the Hanukkah subject. This is the correct and true way; all the upright shall behold the face of the "Tent of the Torah."
