# And He Drew Near
"Then Judah approached him..." <note>Genesis 44:18</note> and said, "O my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh." Behold, it is well known that the Holy Patriarchs and the Tribes, through their actions—every single deed and every matter they had with the people of the nations of the world—were preparing and awakening a high power and great merit through the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "רוח הקודש" (Ruach HaKodesh)</note> within them. By this, they would conquer and subdue the **Prince** <term>Prince: *Sar*, the guardian angel or spiritual representative assigned to a specific nation in Jewish mysticism.</term> of that nation and prevail over him. Consequently, the person below, who is under the dominion of that "Prince," would also be subdued. 

In truth, when Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob went to the land of Egypt or to the other nations and saw that there was a certain "Prince" appointed over them, and saw the evil deeds of those nations, they said: "How is it possible for the Prince of Holiness to rule over such an impure crown and such filth?" Through this precise scrutiny and observation, the "Prince" of that nation was subdued before the **Exalted Prince of Holiness**. By these means, the nations and the "Prince" below were also subdued and would perform acts of **Kindness** <note>original: "חסד" (Chesed)</note> for the Patriarchs. 

In this way, we also explained what we find regarding the **Holy Temple** <note>original: "בית המקדש" (Beit HaMikdash)</note>—may it be rebuilt speedily in our days, Amen—and the holy Altar and the sacrifices that were offered there. Those who looked toward the "Eye of Holiness" and Awe would cause the Altar to rise and offer up [the sacrifice], and the Priest performing the offering would fulfill the Divine Will. However, due to the destruction of the Holy Temple—may it be rebuilt speedily in our days, Amen—on account of our many sins, the Altar no longer stands and no Priest performs such service. Rachel said before the Blessed Lord: "I know that Your jealousy is very strong, especially regarding the matter of **Idolatry** <note>original: "עבודה זרה" (Avodah Zarah)</note>," as mentioned in the **Holy Zohar** <term>Zohar: *Zohar HaKadosh*, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah).</term>. Yet, before the Blessed Lord, there is no jealousy or envy; rather, His mercy is now upon Your precious servants who wait and hope every single day. 

On this day, make known to us our covenant and Your famous kindness to our fathers and to us, and bring us close today to the **Complete Redemption**. And the Lord shall be King over all the earth. As for what is said, "For you are like Pharaoh," this refers to the Exalted One who **atones** <note>The author makes a wordplay between "Pharaoh" and "Kapparah" (atonement/covering).</note> for the Name through the attribute of our Blessed Creator's atonement, and the submission to the Altar and the sacrifices. The Altar was an atonement for sin, as we say in the **Talmud** <note>original: "גמרא" (Gemara)</note>: "At times the Altar provides atonement..." and because of this, there will be more and more kindness upon us. We have explained that when the Messiah comes, there will be joy and gladness of heart, a great joy that is destined to come from the **Exalted Wisdom**

<column-break/>

[The Exalted] Holiness. Through this, the **Holy Greatness** was drawn down from the attribute of the **Exalted Kindness** <note>original: "מדת החסד העליונה" (Midat HaChesed HaElyonah)</note>. For its sake, it is said: "For He delights in kindness," meaning that even though there are "accusers" and "great deceivers" as mentioned above, who act as hindrances, how shall the flow of influence and joy reach those pure righteous ones who cleave to the Lord? Blessed is He, the One who shines from above, for "Merciful God" is His name, His glory, and His place; He awakens grace and compassion upon them with the light of His Blessed Countenance. This is the "Last One" and the "One who fears Heaven." 

The author himself said that within the **Teachings of Chassidism** <term>Chassidism: *Torat HaChassidut*, the mystical and pietistic movement founded by the Baal Shem Tov in the 18th century.</term>, kindness is the foundation, for "there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life forevermore." May those who yearn be [blessed] through the merit of Jacob, who was the most "perfect" among the Patriarchs, the end, the model, and the essence. They said: "Let your honor be..." which means that "the face of Moses was like the face of the sun." The main thing is the Honor/Glory. "And the sun shall rise upon her," the Prophet said, and the good reward shall be paid, and they shall "shine like the stars forever and ever." 

The intention of our Sages, of blessed memory, was to mention the matter of Moses throughout the entire Torah. May He, Blessed be He, merit us to behold the pleasantness of His face, and grant us the "openings of His mouth" to bless and reward. "May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our fathers." Behold our desire; look well upon this good thing. May the Lord help us and lead us to understand the words of Torah, and to keep and guard them in all their ways. May He grant a blessing to the House of Israel, that they may merit forever. And a redeemer shall come to Zion, Amen, and may it be His will, Amen, our God and the God of our fathers.

# And Jacob Lived
"And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years." <note>Genesis 47:28</note> Our Sages, of blessed memory, have already asked regarding this **Torah Portion** <note>original: "פרשה" (Parashah)</note>: Why is it "closed"? <note>A "closed" portion (*Parashah Stumah*) in a Torah scroll lacks the usual paragraph spacing, starting immediately after the previous word.</note> Because all the troubles of the world were closed off and hidden from him. 

The matter is this: "And there was life in the land of Egypt"—meaning the **Holy Vitality** that our father Jacob, peace be upon him, possessed even in the Egyptian exile. He lived with a great measure of vitality, and the Exalted Holiness illuminated him greatly. This was especially true regarding the higher part of the soul, which is the "addition" received on the **Sabbath** and **Holidays**. This is the secret... see what I have written regarding this in the "Source of Life" concerning the daily offering, and when God created the partnership...

### Va’era
<note>The title of the Torah portion in Exodus 6:2, meaning "And I Appeared"</note>

### On Repentance through Love and the Freedom of Purim

Know that on a single day when a person achieves Repentance <note>original: "Teshuvah," the act of returning to God</note>... his heart shall be diligently set toward perfection. Everything follows the path of action, and there is no fear therein, God forbid; it is a path of voluntary choice. One who speaks must look into how the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> and prophecy manifest on that day through metaphor and connection. From this perspective, there is neither compulsion nor necessity, but rather a Repentance born of action. Take it according to the deeds of the teacher, for it is possible to lean upon this. Therefore, this matter exists without the lack of freedom on this day.

On the **Day of Atonement** <note>original: "Yom Ha-Kippurim"</note>, it appeared—and how right it is—that the freedom of the day of **Purim** <note>The holiday celebrating the salvation of the Jews in Persia, characterized by joy</note> comes from the power of thought and contemplation. It has already been seen that on the day of Purim, one should not be afraid, but rather possess only the fear of the "King, the Living and Eternal God." This is the "Crown of the Sea," and without this, it is of no use. This is the reason why awe itself is beneficial; for a person is not coerced by pleasure. Pleasure belongs to the Attribute of Justice <note>term: "Middat Ha-Din" — the aspect of God that governs through strict law and consequence</note>, and it is a complete pleasure that has no fear within it, God forbid.

This is the essence of perfection and the excellence of action: that all those who are exempt should act out of a "continuous love," the love of the Lord. To strengthen themselves in goodness, which is the perfection of the Talmud <note>original: "Gemara"</note>, it dwells in the souls of man. From there, they cast on the garments of joy, gladness, Repentance, and love. If so, a person casts away fear and anxiety and calls it "The Repentance of Freedom" and "Love in the Heart." From there, he casts forth the awakening Repentance; for without the words of the soul, the world of spiritual matters cannot exist. With Repentance, it is possible that even when words and accounts are seen regarding a single soul, there should at least be fear of His Name—fear of judgment, fear of reincarnation <note>original: "gilgul"</note>, and merit. Yet, because of this fear, one is not in a state of joy. Therefore, "look upon man and return in Repentance," which is close to complete joy. 

Understanding <note>original: "Binah," often associated with the "World of Repentance" in Kabbalah</note> is secondary and teaches for all times of the year about the hope that existed in the wisdom and understanding of the German lands <note>original: "Ashkenaz"</note>. Here is the true perfection: regarding the "righteous and upright," here is complete freedom. This is why the Sages of Blessed Memory ordained that on Purim we eat a "commanded feast" <note>original: "Se'udat Mitzvah"</note> and bless the Judgment. If so, it appears that through thought, you see this great hint: the faithful Kindness <note>original: "Chesed"</note> that shines. This is the Repentance of holy and wealthy tranquility. For the days of the heart are joyful, and this is the Holy One, Blessed be He. This is the great sprinkling. Surely there is the sanctity of the Sabbath, which was sanctified in the Sanctuary and the Book of Remembrance, a spirit of satisfaction. And regarding what Rashi <note>the preeminent medieval commentator</note> of blessed memory wrote, he initially asked two things: for on Purim in the Land of Israel in our time, at the time of the Holy One, his soul... and one great final thing as an instruction...

His perfection shall be his constant intention. The moral instruction and the intention in this are dependent [on this]. The essence of his intention and his soul in all movements should be to intend for this Repentance with all the heart—not turning away, nor seeking, nor resembling the attribute of pride.

For such is the awe... and for this thought and action, they shall be like the "teeth of the heart" <note>an anatomical/metaphorical reference to internal grinding or processing</note> from the thought of the cycle of building found within the heights. One should have intention in this without fear of Judgment or the bitterness of Judgment. Fear belongs to the "Repentance of the fear of Judgment," and therefore it is not in the [same] connection. 

The perfection of pleasure on the day of Purim is precious, for on that day the **Secret of the Unity of A-B** <note>term: "Sod Yichud A-B" — likely referring to the union of the kabbalistic partzufim (Divine personas) of Father (Abba) and Daughter/Kingdom (Bat/Malchut)</note> was handed over. The usual merit is that the signs of separation and the removal of the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> are restored and sanctified. The name "Lord God" <note>Adonai Elohim</note> from there left the domain of Purgatory <note>original: "Gehenna"</note> to the will of immortality. For the intention is not proud for this Repentance, which is called by the name **Redemption** <note>original: "Geulah"</note>. 

Regarding this, our Sages of Blessed Memory said: "Our deeds are strong during the festivals of the year." With this thought, which is precious as the intention of the Torah, love is explicitly stated. In any case, through participation, they were in Kindness and the fortune of Holy Redemption. Salvation is like the wine of secrets <note>note: "Yayin" (wine) and "Sod" (secret) both have the numerical value of 70 in Hebrew gematria</note>. From the side of the Supernal Kindness, the heart's intention is focused on this unique matter. This is "eternal freedom," as our Sages of Blessed Memory said: "A free man is one who engages in Torah." We find on Purim that the decree of Judgment was remembered; and if it were a decree that could not be nullified, then one could not pass against the Attribute of Justice. But on the strength of this, there is no longer fear of Judgment. This was their miracle. 

From the perspective of the Glory of the Lord, the pious one said that it is right for this Repentance to exist while there is "freedom in the heart," where there is no fear or dread, God forbid. How great is the goodness for the righteous! The love of the Most High is the love of all creatures, as agreed upon by perfection, the attribute of understanding, and joy in the "joy of a commandment" <note>original: "Simchat Mitzvah"</note>. This perfection comes of itself in the spirit of completeness. When love is revealed, the thought is sanctified without fear, and one turns to Him—that it should be like the Eve of Sabbath, entirely good. Happy is he, and it is good to serve Him.

It is like the eyes, which possess both an **Inner Light** and a **Surrounding Light**. # Page 193

"The mercies of the Lord never cease, for His compassions fail not." <note>original: "Chasdei Hashem ki lo tamnu..." quoting Lamentations 3:22</note> Decrees are sometimes general and sometimes specific; some are carried out through a messenger and others by the Blessed One Himself. After having mentioned the matter of **Individual Providence** <term>Hashgacha Peratit: The belief that God intervenes in the lives of individuals, not just entire species</term>, let us return to discuss the matter of the Divine decree and trial, and the nature of **Free Choice** <term>Bechirah: The human capacity to choose between good and evil</term> which exists among men in both perfection and deficiency. We shall begin by explaining the matter of absolute Divine knowledge and how it does not contradict the concept of human choice and man being free in all his actions—specifically that which is performed by the intellect and the soul.

<margin>The soul lives and all</margin>
->The first order of the second discourse from the *Book of the Soul*<-
->The living soul in man is half from below and half from above so that he may be free to choose life<-
->and the good, or death and the evil<-

Behold, material forms are nothing but a passing shadow, and the soul in the body is like a reflection in a mirror. Now that we have mentioned the "First Order" which is unique to man through wisdom and intellect, we shall return to explain the matter of the temperament and the element found in man, and how they act upon him through his intellect and his **Speaking Soul** <term>Nefesh HaMedabberet: A philosophical term for the rational or human soul that distinguishes humans from animals</term>. For when the soul is moved by intellectual examination, it may perhaps comprehend the Blessed Creator. This is given to man in his "measure" so that the Blessed One has the power to rouse him to action, ensuring that governance is not by necessity, or in a forced, powerful, and coerced manner. Therefore, man was given complete choice and total freedom. General and specific governance is for the purpose of goodness, the preservation of that goodness, and the pursuit of life and existence. The pursuit of death and destruction has no place in man’s true destiny. The **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah: The indwelling presence of God in the world</term> shall be with him and dwell within him, in the sense that the Divine Glory will be within man, providing the vitality of the spirit and the soul. The absolute decree—the very essence of the decree—is the decree that man should be free in that absolute choice of his intellect and his soul. From these significant matters, we can prove the existence of the soul and the life of the **World to Come** <note>original: "Olam HaBa"</note> for the absolute intellectual soul, which is not subject to the accidents of the body and is eternal in its existence before the Blessed Creator, may His name be exalted forever and for all eternity, Amen.

<column-break/>

<margin>And through this it will be clarified</margin>
Here is the existence of Judgment. Those wicked ones <unclear>found</unclear> after a person's death are the forces of impurity that surround the soul and cause it distress. The difference and separation between the wicked and the righteous at the time of their passing is like the difference between light and darkness. For the righteous person merits sublime visions and celestial pleasantness, while the wicked person faces darkness and suffering. All of this is a result of his deeds and actions in this world. As the Blessed One said: "See, I have set before you today life and good..." <note>original: "Re'eh natati lefanecha hayom et hachayim v'et hatov..." quoting Deuteronomy 30:15</note>

<margin>And this refers to a man who performed the commandments for the sake of Heaven</margin>
->The second level is the level of choice of the will<-
->Found in the Speaking Soul<-

Behold, the second level is the level of the choice of the will, which concerns the governance of the body and soul from which actual deeds emerge. All of this comes through wisdom and the soul. Man has absolute freedom in his actions, whether for good or for better, and there is no compulsion in this at all from Heaven. For if there were compulsion or an absolute decree that man could not change, there would be no reward or punishment. The **Practical Intellect** and the **Theoretical Intellect** <term>Sekhel Ma'asi and Sekhel Iyyuni: Medieval philosophical terms for the mind's ability to act in the world versus its ability to contemplate abstract truths</term> are the tools with which man examines and understands his ways. Man's choice and the guidance of the intellect are what lead him to the good, straight, and correct path, which is the path of the commandments. However, the Theoretical Intellect relates to the eternal essence of the soul, which is a "portion of God from above." Man was created from the dust and is formed from matter, but he contains a holy soul which is an emanation from the supernal spirituality. All of this is according to the opinion of the philosophers and the Sages of Truth. Intellectual governance is the absolute perfection of man. In the book *Duties of the Heart* <note>original: "Chovot HaLevavot," an 11th-century work of Jewish philosophy by Bahya ibn Paquda</note>, it is said that man was created with two opposing forces: <unclear>intellect and desire</unclear>...

->**Here in Ferrara, may God protect it**<-

### The Ninth Aspect
The ninth aspect is that of the **Intellect** <term>Sekhel: In medieval Jewish philosophy, this refers to the Cosmic or Active Intellect, the bridge between God and human reason</term>, which possesses sides and eight corners and eighteen "legs." The explanation is that the five angles are situated upon the **Foundation** <term>Yesod: The ninth Sefirah (Divine attribute) in Kabbalah, acting as a channel or "funnel" that gathers Divine light to pass it to the world below</term>, though it is not visible within the Foundation itself. This is called the **Axis** <term>Kotev: The central point or "pole" around which the spheres of the universe or the structures of the mind revolve</term>, through which all intellect understands.

Behold, the measure of each side of these three is a quarter of **Ten** <note>original: "Yod," the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often symbolizing the point of creation or the Sefirah of Wisdom</note>. Each side shall be six thousand, four hundred and eighty cubits. Thus, between them are fourteen thousand, eight hundred and eighty cubits. The meaning of this is that it represents the **"Half-Whole"** <note>original: "Chatzi ha-Shalem"</note>. The calculation and form of the Half-Whole point toward the laws and the rectitude of the name of **Justice** <term>Tzedek: Often associated with the Sefirah of Malchut (Kingship) and the moon, representing Divine law reflected in the world</term>. Through this, every knower of understanding may comprehend the width and the line of the "Tablets" and the **Radiance of the Mirrors** <note>original: "Ziv ha-Mar'ot"</note>.

Just as a person sees themselves in a mirror, so too the Intellect is indicated by the Names within it. This is like the speech of a person to their companion; so too is it with the Blessed Lord. Every word and action is considered the power of **Formulation** <term>Tziyur: The mental ability to visualize or "draw" an idea in the mind before it is acted upon</term> and measurement. These are the matters indicated by the **Honored Name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHVH</note>; according to its greatness, the Honored Name indicates the nature of the Intellect.

Behold, the **Root Names** <note>original: "Shemot ha-Mekoriyim"</note> are numbered at sixteen. These names encompass every quality and every form of action. Within this portion lies the grace of His kindness, His form, and His might. From Him is everything, and to Him everything is forever committed. Happy is the eye that has seen this! For the Blessed Name has hinted at the **Perfect Intellect**, which is **Kingship** <term>Malchut: The final Sefirah, representing the Divine Presence or Shekhinah as it dwells within the physical world</term> uniting with the portion of the Intellect, may He be blessed and exalted. These are the names called within the **Perfect Form** <note>original: "Tziyur ha-Shalem"</note>. What the Intellect hinted at through the form of the body and the heights—the Supernal Intellect and the Supernal Radiance—these are all names hinting at the Intellect, blessed be He. These are the names of the attributes of the Intellect according to its parts and its praises. In the standing of the Intellect in the high station and its rectitude, it is perfect without deficiency; all its parts unite with one another and shall not be separated. This matter and this path are simple: it is **Justice**, it is the **Supernal Kingship**, and the **Radiance of the Splendor** <note>original: "Ziv ha-Zohar"</note> of the Righteous One, may His name be blessed, Amen Selah.

# The Additional Soul of the Sabbath

It is for man to be an investigator of every action and matter within the order of preeminence and standing. Through this, he will understand that it is within his power to do good and to act according to his will, following the designated excellence. From this level, the **Fear of Sin** <term>Yirat Chet: a high level of piety where one fears the distance from God caused by sin</term> is in the heart of any God-fearing man; he shall not come to the sin of [disrupting] any order of the orders of the world. If so, the awe of the Creator of the world is a regular portion in every heart. This fear of the "tread of judgment" is what makes the one who acts in this way possess superior conduct. Within it, for the children of men, is "Eternal Kindness," and from them comes the Order of Human Morality. These are the waves of the **Exalted Chariot** <term>Merkavah: the "Divine Chariot" or throne-world; here it refers to man becoming a vehicle for divine presence through his actions</term> which connects to him through the act of conduct. He proceeds, which is to say, in superior conduct.

<meta>The previous page appears to have concluded a discussion on the soul of the Torah or transitioned from a different language (Syriac/Arabic), as noted in the previous record. # On Free Will and Divine Foreknowledge

## The Nature of Human Agency

When a person senses fear in their heart, they might say: "What is the purpose of this fear? Perhaps I have sinned?" This is because man is a "possessor of choice" <term>Hebrew: *ba'al bechira*; the capacity for autonomous moral decision-making</term>, whether he performs a sin or a commandment. Man possesses complete free will, just as the Scripture states: "Behold, the man has become like one of us, to know good and evil" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>. Every single day, the choice is in his hands. 

It is indeed true that His knowledge <note>referring to God</note>, may He be blessed, preceded all things; nevertheless, choice remains in the hands of man. As Maimonides <note>original: *HaRambam* (1138–1204), Rabbi Moses ben Maimon, the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> of blessed memory wrote: it is impossible for human intellect to fully comprehend how God's foreknowledge and man's choice coexist, yet it is a clear and certain truth that choice is in the hands of man. The commentators have discussed this at length, particularly the author of the *Akedat Yitzchak* <note>original: *Baal HaAkeidah*, Rabbi Isaac Arama (15th century), a Spanish Jewish philosopher and commentator.</note>. Scripture says: "And behold, the Lord stood over him..." <note>Genesis 28:13</note>; He, may He be blessed, looks into the heart of man, whether for good or for evil, at every moment and every second.

---

I have further stated regarding the reason for Free Choice that man was created from both a soul and a body. Just as the soul originates from the Upper World, the body originates from the Lower World. Man stands as the intermediary between the two, and he is a "possessor of choice" to incline himself toward the side of good or the side of evil. Since he contains these two opposing forces within him, the choice is in his hands. 

This is like a parable of a king who sent two ministers to a single city; he commanded one to act in one way, and the other to act in another. Man is the one who decides between them. This is the "secret of choice" <term>Hebrew: *sod ha-bechira*; the deeper mystical or philosophical logic behind human agency</term>. It is as written in the Holy Zohar <note>folio 213a</note> using the parable of the man and the dog: the dog wants to eat from the table, but the master of the house prevents it. So it is with the Evil Inclination <term>Hebrew: *Yetzer HaRa*; the innate human impulse toward selfishness or sin</term>. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "If the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not help him, he could not overcome it" <note>A Talmudic phrase suggesting that while man chooses to resist evil, he requires divine assistance to succeed</note>; this is sufficient for the wise.

---

In the *Midrash Rabbah* <note>An ancient collection of homiletical interpretations of the Torah</note> on the portion of *Vayechi*, they interpreted the verse: "Issachar is a strong-boned donkey" <note>Genesis 49:14</note>. They explained that the Torah was given to the children of Issachar because they were "those who had understanding of the times" <note>1 Chronicles 12:32</note>. They possessed the power of understanding to recognize the times and seasons—when it is a time for good and when it is a time for evil—and they chose the good. This is also the essence of choice: for a person must recognize the times and seasons.

<column-break/>

## Resolving the Paradox of Foreknowledge

With this, we can answer the difficulty raised by the *Maggid Mishneh* <note>original: *HaRav HaMaggid*, Rabbi Vidal de Tolosa (14th century), a major commentator on Maimonides' legal code.</note> in the first part of the "Laws of Repentance" <note>Hilkhot Teshuvah, Chapter 5, Law 5</note>. He questioned Maimonides' statement that Divine knowledge and human choice are not contradictory. Since God's knowledge is simply the reality of how a thing exists, if a thing were to happen differently, His knowledge would likewise have been different. Therefore, His knowledge does not "cause" the choice at all. 

However, the *Maggid Mishneh* challenged him, arguing that knowledge nonetheless implies necessity <note>If God knows X will happen, then X *must* happen, otherwise God's knowledge was incorrect.</note>. He wrote: "What you should know is that God's knowledge is not something additional to His essence... He and His knowledge are one. Just as it is impossible to perceive the essence of the Creator, so it is impossible to perceive His knowledge." Yet the *Maggid Mishneh* concludes that this is not a sufficient answer, for it remains a necessity that if His knowledge encompasses all things before they exist, then the thing must necessarily occur that way. If it is not necessary, His knowledge would not be "truthful," Heaven forbid.

The author of the *Pnei Yehoshua* <note>original: *Pnei Yehoshua*, Rabbi Jacob Joshua Falk (1680–1756), a famous Talmudic analyst.</note>, in his insights on the tractate *Bava Metzia* <note>folio 94a</note>, discussed this at length. He wrote: "It is certain that the intention is that the Name, may He be blessed, created man to be a 'possessor of choice' to act according to his will." Since man is a complete possessor of choice, the action is in his hand to do as he desires, and God's knowledge does not impose necessity at all. 

This is what Maimonides meant by saying we lack the power to perceive His knowledge. The intent is that the Creator, may He be blessed, embedded it in the nature of man to be a "possessor of choice." This is the "Divine power" <term>Hebrew: *koach Eloki*</term> within him. Just as His knowledge is with Him, so too the power of choice is in the nature of man by virtue of the soul within him, which is a "portion of God from above." Through this, we can explain what is written in the holy books: "The righteous man decrees, and the Holy One fulfills." Since the righteous man is a complete possessor of choice, he rules over his own nature.

<summary>This page explores the theological paradox of how human free will can coexist with God's perfect foreknowledge. The author synthesizes views from Maimonides and later commentators, arguing that free choice is a divine, innate power granted to the human soul.</summary>
<keywords>Free Will, Divine Foreknowledge, Maimonides, Pnei Yehoshua, Issachar, Evil Inclination, soul and body, Jewish Philosophy, Maggid Mishneh, Akedat Yitzchak</keywords>

# On the Order of Torah Reading

And this is what Maimonides <note>original: *HaRambam* (1138–1204), a foundational scholar of Jewish law</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in the eighth chapter of the *Laws of Prayer*: "One must not have fewer than seven readers [on the Sabbath]..." etc. This implies that the requirement is not strictly due to the "honor of the Sabbath" <note>original: *kavod Shabbat*; a legal principle requiring extra dignity for the holy day</note>, but rather it is an intrinsic requirement of the Sabbath day itself. [See] Tractate Berakhot, page 21b, and in the *Gemara* <note>the part of the Talmud containing rabbinic analysis</note> there, we find that he would not say "and this" but rather he would say "and this."
M. P. A. T. E. T. L. PM. <note>Likely a mnemonic or acronym for the order of specific liturgical verses or names, common in manuscript margins.</note>

<column-break/>

Before I return to investigate whether one is permitted to ascend to the Torah scroll <term>Aliyah: the honor of being called to recite a blessing over the Torah</term> on the Sabbath with fewer than seven [readers], or on a Festival <note>original: *Yom Tov*</note> with fewer than five, or on a New Moon <note>original: *Rosh Chodesh*</note> and the intermediate days of a festival with fewer than four:

I saw in the *Order of Prayer* <note>Siddur</note> of my master and teacher, the eminent and pious Rabbi Zechariah, of blessed memory, who wrote that anything possessing two designations—such as "the honor of the Sabbath" and "the honor of the Torah"—allows for additions to be made to both as one desires. Furthermore, he wrote in the name of Rabbi Abraham, of blessed memory, that we say in the *Gemara*, and Rashi <note>the primary medieval commentator on the Talmud</note> explained as follows:

One must examine what we say at the beginning of Tractate Megillah: "One may not have fewer than seven [readers], and one may not add to them." This implies that on the Sabbath, one should not add [to the number of readers]. However, have we not learned in the *Gemara* of Megillah (page 23a and 21b), where it is taught: "Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar says: On every Sabbath and Festival that does not have an Additional Service <note>original: *Musaf*; the extra sacrifice or prayer for holy days</note>, we read [with] eight [people]..." etc.? And on page 23a, it is taught: "Rabbi Akiva says: On every Sabbath and Festival that has an Additional Service, we read [with] seven." And on page 21b, it is taught that Rabbi Akiva says... etc. And in Tractate Megillah there, Rav Huna says: "We read [with] seven, corresponding to the seven prophets..." etc. And on page 23a, it is taught that Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar says: "On every Sabbath and Festival that has an Additional Service, we read [with] seven, and on a Sabbath without an Additional Service, we read [with] eight." And on page 21b, it is taught: "Rabbi Akiva says: Seven." 

We see from this that in every case there is a dispute regarding this matter. In the final conclusion of the *Gemara* in Megillah, we say: "On the Sabbath we read [with] seven, on the Day of Atonement <note>original: *Yom Kippur*</note> [with] six, and on a Festival [with] five." And we say in the *Gemara* on page 23a: "Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar says..." etc. Rather, that which Rav Huna said—that seven corresponds to the seven prophets—refers specifically to the Sabbath, where there are seven called to the Torah; however, on other days, there is no need for seven.

There in the *Gemara*, it states the general rule: "Whenever there is a neglect of work for the people <note>original: *bitul melakha*; the concern that a long service would hinder the community's livelihood</note>, such as a Fast Day or the Ninth of Av, we read [with] three. On a New Moon and the intermediate days of a festival where there is an Additional Sacrifice, we read [with] four. On a Festival, five. On the Day of Atonement, six. On the Sabbath, seven." One may not have fewer than these, but one may add to them. As for the teaching "one may not add to them," that follows Rav Huna, who said the number corresponds to the seven prophets. Thus it was taught: "This is the rule..." etc. And there we say: "On the Sabbath we read [with] seven; Rav Huna said this corresponds to the seven prophets." Then it asks a difficulty from that which was taught by Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar... etc. From this we see that on the Sabbath, one *does* add. Rav Huna only spoke of the other days, where one does not add, but on the Sabbath, one may add. And that which we say in Megillah, Chapter 3, page 23a—"On the Sabbath we read [with] seven and do not add to them"—is specifically according to Rav Huna's view because of the seven prophets; however, we learn from this that it is indeed appropriate to add [if one wishes].

<summary>This page analyzes the legal requirements for the number of people called to the Torah on various holy days, debating whether the number seven for the Sabbath is a fixed limit or a minimum.</summary>
